steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Zinc concentrate
form.label: a few hundred grams of germanium a tonne at best

steps.text: Germanium has no ore of its own. It hides in sphalerite, the main zinc mineral, at a few hundred grams a tonne in the richer deposits, and in some coals. It is recovered only as a by-product.
in: Hidden in zinc ores and some coals

steps.title: Ride with zinc
steps.text: Zinc ore is mined and floated to a concentrate, which goes to a zinc smelter. Germanium ends up in the residues left when the zinc is leached out. In China, germanium-rich lignite is burnt and the germanium collected from the fly ash.
steps.india: No Indian zinc smelter runs a germanium recovery circuit.

steps.title: Extract
steps.text: The residue is leached and the germanium precipitated as a crude concentrate. This is reacted with hydrochloric acid to make germanium tetrachloride, a liquid that boils at 84°C, so it can be distilled away from everything else.

steps.title: Refine
steps.text: The tetrachloride is reacted with water to give germanium dioxide, a white powder, which is reduced with hydrogen to metal. Bars of metal are zone-refined: a molten band is swept along the bar, carrying impurities to one end. China refines 70 to 80% of the world's germanium.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: The tetrachloride itself goes to fibre makers, who add it to the glass core of optical fibre. The dioxide becomes a catalyst for PET plastic. The metal is grown into crystals and cut into lenses, windows and wafers.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Germanium keeps light inside optical fibre, and germanium lenses are transparent to heat, so they are the eyes of thermal cameras and night-vision sights. Germanium wafers carry the solar cells on most satellites.
steps.india: Defence optics, fibre and space demand, all imported.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Fibre and lens making waste much of the germanium they start with, and that scrap is routinely recovered. Decommissioned thermal optics are also reclaimed.

sources.title: Takshashila, India Critical Minerals: scores, project records and capability notes (2026)
